ownership_reason: Only the gold sees the final group of the magnitude bytes together with the number of bytes it holds and the positions of its four characters; hops 1-4 pass whole arrays (the magnitude bytes, the standard alphabet) and get back the whole encoded array, and no input they can pass makes a final single-byte group keep its two characters (zero-extending or left-padding the bytes, or another alphabet, changes the characters themselves). The gold's javadoc promises the encoding of the bytes using the base64 algorithm; for 64 magnitude bytes (a final group of one byte) the base64 encoding ends in two characters and "==" (...Yjg==), which the variant does not produce (...Yj===). The convention is pinned outside the gold: Base64.encode(byte[], int, int), the streaming encoder behind Base64.encodeBase64 and BCodec.doEncoding, writes two characters and then PAD twice for a final single byte ('case 1') and three characters and PAD once for two ('case 2'); Base64Test testSingletons ("AA==", "AQ==", ...), testKnownEncodings ("...Lg==", "...cw==") and testPairs ("AAA=") pass; testCodeInteger1, testCodeInteger2 and testCodeInteger4 pass through the same chain with final groups of two bytes.
